svg.title: Three levels of text representation
svg.desc: Kintsch's three levels for one sentence about a supplier's price rise: the surface code of exact words, the textbase of stated propositions, and the situation model that adds the reader's knowledge and inferences. Elaboration operates mainly at the situation-model level.
svg.text: Three levels at which a sentence can be represented
Text: "The supplier raised prices by 8%. Margins on the premium range fell."
"The supplier raised prices by 8%. Margins on the premium range fell."
Fades within seconds to minutes; supports verbatim recall only.
Supports summary and recall of what the text said; the link between
the two sentences is not stated, only implied.
SITUATION MODEL - the state of affairs the text describes

g.text: Bridging inference: the price rise CAUSED the margin fall.
Elaborative inference: the premium range probably relies more on this supplier.
Prior knowledge: if a firm cannot raise its own prices, cost rises come out of margin.
Prediction: unless prices rise or the supplier changes, margins stay down next quarter.

svg.text: After Walter Kintsch's construction-integration model; proposition notation simplified.
